newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: A hefty corporate order for dollars thwarted the rand's attempt to move below the 4.54 level on Friday.
It settled at 4.5510/5560, fractionally firmer than its 4.5515/5565 finish on Thursday.
The rand started the day looking to probe below the 4.54 level, trading at a day's best level of 4.5390 about 10 minutes before the market officially opened.
After initially appearing to be long of dollars, dealer said the market had actually gone short, and was caught offguard by a large local corporate order for dollars.
"A fairly large importer came in at 4.5450 when the market had gone short," a dealer said, adding that the order had been followed by steady importer demand for the rest of the day.
"It was one-way traffic all the way up...and there was not much supply at the top," he said.
Offshore interest was limited and volumes were generally described as healthy.
The rand came in for another pasting from the pound on the day, as cable extended its weeklong gains to a fresh 12-month high.
The British currency's resurgence was pinned on UK press reports that the Treasury was planning to hike interest rates by a full percentage point.
The rand touched a worst-ever level of 7.2513 against sterling from 7.2036/2161 overnight, while against the mark it was last quoted at 0.3383/3389 from 0.3391/3396 previously.
On the bond market, yields spent the day tracking the rand's movements as well as the stronger U.S. Treasury bond market.
The key R150 was last pegged at a yield of 15.31 percent, little changed from Thursday's 15.315 percent finish.
Dealers said trade was mostly two-way and jobber-driven.
"It was mainly longs cutting and shorts covering their positions ahead of the weekend," a dealer said.

He said most players had preferred to go home square at the weekend, in case an important announcement was made at a press conference being held by IMF managing director Michel Camdessus and South African Finance Minister Trevor Manuel in Cape Town at 1530 GMT.

Dealers said that while speculation that the press conference would be used to announce the lifting of some of the country's remaining exchange controls had dimmed, it was still at the back of some people's minds.
On the money market, three-month NCDs quoted steady at between 16.10 percent bid and 15.95 percent, while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at between 15.55 and 15.35 percent.
The Reserve Bank indicated the daily shortage at 7.300 billion rand on Thursday from 7.612 billion rand on Wednesday.
Bond Exchange figures show foreigners sold a net 168.48 million rand worth of South African bonds on Thursday after buying a net 71.36 million rand on Wednesday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 33.83 billion rand on Thursday -- a settlement day -- from 4.22 billion rand on Wednesday.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
